subject: Resilience offset package proposal and exec approval request — Globex latency incident
messages:
From: Amelia Chen <amelia@globex.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Repeated latency — request for remediation/compensation

Hi Vanessa,

We saw repeated 99th-percentile latency spikes across our production inference endpoints on 2027-08-06 and again on 2027-08-07. The incidents caused a handful of user-facing timeouts in our billing flow and one partner webhook retry loop. Our infra team attached a short trace to this note.

Can you share Redwood's incident report and outline what remediation you propose? Given the impact we expect some form of credit or a one-time concession; please propose something concrete and a timeline for us to get it closed.

Thanks,
Amelia Chen
Senior Engineering Manager — Payments
Globex Corporation

Attachment: globex-trace-0807.json (log excerpt)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Chen <amelia@globex.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Repeated latency — request for remediation/compensation

Hi Amelia — thanks for the note and the trace. I’m really sorry this affected the billing flow; I appreciate you flagging it quickly. We’ve run a post-mortem and attached a concise incident report (slo-incident-report-2027-08.pdf). High level: a misrouted routing policy triggered resource contention in a subset of Dedicated workers during a regional deploy, which produced tail latency > SLO for ~45 minutes each day. The root cause is fixed and we’ve pushed a configuration safeguard to prevent recurrence.

Proposed remediation: before I propose anything official I want to align with my team and finance/legal, but here’s a customer-oriented package I think is fair and quick to deliver:
- Two months of a 12.5% invoice credit applied to your September and October invoices (to reflect reduced availability during the incident window)
- One-time compute credit of $35,000 (usable for model inference or dedicated burst capacity)
- A collaborative review of routing & cache configuration with our infra engineers (1 session + runbook updates)

I’ve attached the internal proposal workbook (resilience-offset-proposal-vanessa.xlsx). Please let me know if that high-level package would work for Globex and I’ll route for approval. If you prefer a different structure (larger single credit vs months), say so and we’ll adapt.

Sincerely,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: slo-incident-report-2027-08.pdf; resilience-offset-proposal-vanessa.xlsx
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec approval request — Globex resilience offset package (incident 2027-08-06/07)

Marissa / Karthik / Aditya —

Filed the incident report and proposed the package below to Globex (they asked for something concrete). Summary of impact: two ~45-minute tail-latency windows across two days affecting the payments flow; high business risk because of partner webhook retries. Account status: strategic, current ARR $2.4M, up for renewal Q4.

Proposed customer offer (requested via Amelia):
- 12.5% credit applied to invoices for Sep + Oct 2027 (not to exceed credit cap in contract)
- $35,000 one-time compute credit applied to their account (expires 12/31/2028)
- Free joint engineering review + runbook update (2 engineer-hours covered)

Asks:
1) Exec approval to exceed standard credit caps for this one-off (legal caps credits at 10% without exec sign-off) — I’m requesting approval for the 12.5% two-month approach and the $35k compute credit.
2) Finance sign-off on how we apply the credit in HubSpot/billing so it doesn’t count as a refund.
3) If approved, I’ll send a final terms doc via DocuSign; legal will need to review the small amendment.

Attachments: resilience-offset-proposal-vanessa.xlsx (detailed breakdown), incident report.

Notes on equity: I think a slightly higher compute credit (vs a larger percent invoice credit) is better business-wise — it offsets their spend, encourages product usage, and avoids compounding discount risks over renewal.

Thanks for a timely review — their renewal conversation starts in mid-September and we should resolve prior to that.

— Vanessa
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exec approval request — Globex resilience offset package (incident 2027-08-06/07)

Vanessa — reviewed the incident summary and the customer context. I approve an exception to the standard credit cap for this single remediation. Approved terms:
- 15% invoice credit applied across Sep and Oct 2027 (increase from 12.5% given partner impact)
- $50,000 one-time compute credit (move to platform credits, expires 12/31/2028)
- Joint engineering review + a follow-up 30-day post-review report

Conditions:
1) Legal to prepare a short amendment; do not apply credits until legal sign-off and a DocuSign acceptance from Globex.
2) Finance to code the compute credit as platform credit (not paper refund) — Aditya, please coordinate.
3) This approval is one-off for Globex and tied to the incident dates; mark it as a special concession in HubSpot (deal note).

I’ve attached the approved terms doc (approved-offer-terms-marissa.docx). Move forward and loop Legal/Finance; let me know when you have DocuSign ready and I’ll give final sign-off.

— Marissa
